Home, settings, sign-in, profiles, the version picker, the control editor and the in-game menu were redrawn from scratch, designed around what you actually do and built to work one-handed. Settings has a search, so you never have to remember which screen a setting was on.
When the game dies, the log gets read for you and the cause is named in plain words: a missing mod dependency, not enough memory, the wrong Java version. It quotes the line it concluded from.

Performance mode reads what your device actually is, then sets the renderer, the resolution, the memory and Minecraft\'s own graphics settings to match, and offers to install the mods that do the rest. It shows you every change before it makes one.
It never turns a setting back up that you had turned down, and switching it off puts everything back.
